verdict.rationale: Daytona's core product is isolated sandboxes. Each sandbox gets a dedicated kernel, filesystem, network stack and resources, and sits behind a firewall that blocks exfiltration, so it provides true sandbox isolation rather than a dry-run mode. AI agents can create and test in these sandboxes programmatically via the SDKs, CLI and MCP server. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that the isolation holds, and explicit documentation on keeping production data or credentials separate from sandboxes.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: Each sandbox runs in isolation, giving it a dedicated kernel, filesystem, network stack, and allocated vCPU, RAM, and disk.
Each sandbox runs behind a firewall that restricts which external IP addresses and domains it can reach, preventing untrusted code from exfiltrating data or contacting arbitrary hosts.
Sandboxes are isolated runtime environments you can manage programmatically to run code.
Daytona Model Context Protocol (MCP) server enables AI agents to interact with Daytona Sandboxes programmatically.
